name: Isolated Melanotic Schwannoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Melanotic Schwannoma

criteria.description: Presence of spindle-shaped Schwann cells with melanin pigment on histopathology
Positive immunostaining for S-100 protein and HMB-45
MRI showing well-circumscribed pigmented mass with T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of pigmented Schwann cells with positive S-100 and HMB-45 immunostaining
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may be performed to exclude Carney complex in cases with multiple lesions.

pathognomonic.notes: Typically presents as a solitary pigmented mass
searchTerms: nerve sheath tumor with pigment cells

common.symptomName: Localized neurological deficit related to tumor location
common.notes: May include sensory or motor impairment
searchTerms: weakness or numbness from tumor location
tingling or weakness from nerve compression
bright lesion on MRI T1 scan
T1 hyperintense brain or nerve lesion

occasional.symptomName: Mass effect causing adjacent tissue displacement
occasional.notes: Depends on tumor size and location

rare.notes: Only in syndromic cases, not isolated

rare.symptomName: Systemic symptoms such as weight loss or fever
searchTerms: general illness with fever and weight loss
systemic signs like fever and weight loss

laboratory: No specific laboratory abnormalities; routine labs typically normal
imaging: MRI showing well-circumscribed pigmented mass with T1 hyperintensity and T2 hypointensity
CT scan may show soft tissue mass with possible calcifications
genetic: Negative for PRKAR1A mutations in isolated cases (positive in Carney complex-associated cases)
other: Histopathology demonstrating spindle cells with melanin pigment
Immunohistochemistry positive for S-100 protein and HMB-45

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of atypical melanocytes with mitotic figures
Positive for melanocytic markers but lacks Schwann cell features
Different immunohistochemical profile (negative for melanocytic markers)
Typically shows Antoni A and B areas histologically
Histology shows neurofibroma features with melanin pigment
Different clinical presentation and genetic background

redFlags: Evidence of tumor hemorrhage or malignant transformation
references: Carney JA. Melanotic Schwannoma: A Tumor of the Nervous System and Its Relation to Carney Complex. Am J Surg Pathol. 1996.
Rodriguez FJ, Folpe AL. Melanotic Schwannoma: Clinicopathologic Study of 40 Cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2012.
